title: A Archive for the Colony
premise: Hazel Yarrow, a navigator who has spent a decade outrunning the memory of the colonists' backups she helped jettison during the Meridian evacuation, intercepts the Erebus, a ship returned from deep space with its crew aged backward into children carrying adult minds. The message they bring can end the colonial war — but delivering it means exposing that Hazel's old command falsified the evacuation logs, and that the 'backups' in her hold are the war's first casualties, still conscious. Pursued by both fleets and haunted by the child-aged messenger who remembers dying, Hazel must choose between duty to the truth and love for Ilsa Vane, the intelligence officer ordered to silence it. In the end Hazel broadcasts the message and the logs together at terrible cost — sacrificing her own backup continuity — forcing both sides to reckon with what survival has cost them.
about_author: Ines Voss is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years on cargo runs between island ports before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Ten years after the Meridian evacuation, Hazel hauls contraband seed-stock through contested orbits, quietly keeping the hold's dormant backups powered against regulations. A distress ping from an unregistered vessel forces a course change. The emotional beat is guilt worn smooth by routine — until the ping resolves as something impossible: the Erebus, lost forty years ago.

chapters.title: The Children of Erebus
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Boarding the drifting Erebus, Hazel finds a crew aged backward into children with intact adult memories, led by nine-year-old Captain Oren Sato, who recognizes her name from the evacuation logs. They carry a message addressed to both fleets' high commands. The beat is dread: the message references Meridian, and Oren calls her 'the one who signed.'

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vane's POV. Fleet intelligence officer Ilsa Vane boards under pretext of customs inspection, tasked with retrieving the message and erasing everyone aboard. She and Hazel share a history neither will name aloud. Ilsa stalls her own orders while reading the message's header. The beat is divided loyalty sharpening into something more dangerous: recognition.

chapters.title: What Sleeps in the Hold
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. The child-captain discovers the backups in Hazel's hold are Meridian colonists — including his own original body's pattern, recorded mid-death. He confronts Hazel, who confesses she signed the falsified log that abandoned them. The beat is raw confrontation; Oren must decide whether hatred or curiosity drives him now.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Both fleets converge on the Erebus's coordinates, each claiming salvage rights over the ship and its message. Hazel threads a debris field to escape, using navigation tricks from the evacuation she swore never to repeat. Ilsa covers their escape against her own fleet. The beat is exhilaration curdling into commitment — there is no going back.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Survival
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Hiding in a dead station, Ilsa decrypts enough of the message to learn the truth: the war began because Meridian's backers destroyed evidence of the failed backups — evidence Hazel's signature could corroborate. Ilsa must choose between her orders and Hazel. The beat is quiet devastation; love and duty stop being parallel lines.

chapters.title: Oren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. Oren offers Hazel a trade: his testimony in exchange for waking his backup pattern so he can meet the man he was. The awakening half-succeeds, leaving the adult Oren aware only of his death. The boy holds his own dying hand. The beat is grief as inheritance — some knowledge can only be carried, not fixed.

chapters.title: Intercept
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Fleet hunters corner them at the Meridian relay station itself, where the war's first shot was fired. Ilsa's handler demands she execute the erasure order on live comms. Instead Ilsa transmits the message fragment she's verified, making herself a traitor. The beat is the point of no return, paid for in Ilsa's career and freedom.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. To broadcast the full message credibly, Hazel must upload her own command logs — which requires merging with her personal backup, risking overwrite of the woman she has become. With Ilsa anchoring her identity voice-to-voice, Hazel transmits everything: message, logs, confession. The beat is terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: A Archive for the Colony
chapters.summary: Oren's POV, resolution. The broadcast forces an armistice tribunal; the colony's archives open, and the Erebus children become its first living witnesses rather than its erased casualties. Hazel survives diminished — gaps where ten years used to be — and chooses to stay with Ilsa anyway. Oren files the final entry himself. The beat is hard-won peace: survival, honestly priced.
